newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares face computer snags, rise to new high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares face computer snags, rise to new high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices braved computer problems on Monday and rose to a fresh 23-month high in trading that focused on the milling and cement sectors.

Brokers said the Capital Market Authority (CMA) extended bourse trading hours after computer hang-ups hampered trade. But the CMA all-share index managed to rise 0.16 percent to 242.98 points, its highest level since early December 1994.
The computer crash affected turnover, which slipped to 14.74 million pounds ($4.33 million) from Sunday's 20.42 million.

"It was quiet and many brokers were just putting in bids to buy which were not being processed and so increasing prices. But there was also real demand," said broker Rasha Lashin of securities house Hermes-EFG.
Brokers said the milling and cement shares were the most heavily traded and also led the bourse upwards.

Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the day's most active share, rising 0.50 pounds to 51.05 in trading worth 1.14 million pounds. Central and West Delta Flour Mills also gained 0.95 to close at 61.75 pounds.

Egyptian Portland Tora Cement rose 1.00 to 68 pounds after the firm announced on Thursday higher profits for the past 1995/96 financial year. Some demand rubbed off on Suez Cement but the stock ended unchanged at 50 pounds.

Misr Exterior Bank was the day's biggest gainer after a single transaction worth 975,000 pounds hiked share prices 8.33 percent to 650.00 pounds. A select investor group hold the bank's shares and brokers said one shareholder was probably selling his holdings to another.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 361.69 points from Sunday's 361.54 points and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 171.89 from 171.52.
